tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (review, assess, audit, grade a cluster; questions about production readiness, risks, upgrade safety), explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where EKS isn't named directly ('describe Kubernetes workloads on AWS without naming EKS'), and also states a clear negative scope ('Do not use it for a quick ungraded health snapshot or an active incident investigation'). It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriately concise given the complexity of the skill's scope.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when someone wants an Amazon EKS cluster graded against best practices. Use it when they ask to review, assess, audit, or grade a cluster; ... Do not use it for a quick ungraded health snapshot or an active incident investigation.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and largely avoids explaining concepts the agent already knows, which is good, but it is extremely compressed/jargon-heavy in places (e.g., ledger definitions, fingerprint formulas crammed into single sentences), making it harder to parse than necessary. Still, it stays focused on domain-specific procedure rather than general concepts, so this is a minor concern.
tests.evidence: Keep in current context only: confirmed identity/scope/window; 49 area statuses and bounded projections; source attempts; gate decisions; selected/completed units; exact verdicts; FAIL evidence, descriptive severity, canonical resource ID, fingerprint, and remediation route; reference-load audit; QA result; next unit.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not embed large reference tables, API docs, error code tables, or metric thresholds inline; it consistently delegates such detail to references/ files (manifest, thresholds, discovery commands, etc.) and loads them conditionally.
tests.evidence: Per-unit counts and exact ID membership live in `references/runtime/check-manifest.md`; read them there each run.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Several files/directories listed under references/ are never linked with a markdown link pattern '[text](references/filename)' in the body, e.g. aiml-workloads.md, aws-api-checks.md, hybrid-nodes.md, upgrade-readiness.md, windows-workloads.md, and the pillars/ and decision-trees/ directory files other than control-plane.md and api-latency-429.md. Many references are mentioned only as bare filenames without markdown link syntax.
tests.evidence: Windows fires when `windows_nodes>0`; Hybrid when `hybrid_nodes>0`; AI/ML when GPU or Neuron nodes exist; the manifest owns their exact IDs and counts.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (discovery order, fingerprinting, report rendering order) are given exact, prescriptive instructions, while softer judgment areas (gathering context, prioritizing remediation) are described with purpose rather than rigid steps, matching prescriptiveness to fragility well.
tests.evidence: A full review grades exactly 288 core rows; the check manifest owns membership. S7 must PASS before S8.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal options; it mandates a single tool (`use_kubectl`) with a fixed command set, which functions as a clear default/constraint rather than a menu.
tests.evidence: Discovery runs only through the AWS DevOps Agent MCP tool `use_kubectl`: `get`, `describe`, `logs`, `version`, `config current-context`, `cluster-info`, `top`, and `get --raw`, one command per tool call.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable, repeatable grading procedure (discovery, inventory, routing, grading, QA, render) applicable to any EKS cluster, not a one-off declaration for a specific cluster.
tests.evidence: Named requests grade named units; full/CWR grades all nine pillars plus AX.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes substantial gotchas-like guidance throughout (e.g., stop rules, redaction requirements, false-gate handling, empty-query caveats) which function as concrete corrections to likely agent mistakes in this domain.
tests.evidence: Empty query results remain unknown until source, stream, delay, filters, and window are verified.
